_what: Canonical migrations that do not replay onto the 2026-08-19 baseline structure on a plain PostgreSQL 16. Each entry is a measured failure with the migration's own message; up.sh tolerates EXACTLY these and aborts on any other. None touches the trip domain; every trip_* object, the kernel and the projection worker replay cleanly.
_measured: 2026-09-12, local PostgreSQL 16.13 + PostGIS 3.4.2, chain applied from 2093 (the first file whose objects are absent from the baseline; 2092 is the last present). Re-measured 2026-10-06 on CI's postgis/postgis:16-3.4 service container (ci.yml api-server-local-db), chain from 2093 in APPLY order (byte order + src/migrations/ORDER_OVERRIDES.json): 2136_profiles_auth_users_convergence.sql replays in order under the 2136-after-2139 override and was removed; every entry below still fails with the text recorded for it (2140's and 2276's stated CAUSES corrected, their error texts unchanged).
_rule: An entry here is a fact about the replay, not permission to ignore the file. Remove an entry when the file replays; add one only with the verbatim error.

files.2140_deletion_receipt.sql: POSTCONDITION FAILED: status CHECK does not permit 'completed', which AccountDeletionService writes; — NOT 2136's shape, as this entry used to say: measured 2026-10-06 with 2136 replaying cleanly ahead of it, 2140 still fails. The 2026-08-19 baseline is PRODUCTION's structure, whose user_deletion_requests status CHECK lacks 'completed'; portava-ci's CHECK had it all along (2178_deletion_status_check_converge.sql's header records the drift), and 2178 adds it on this harness later in the chain, so up.sh's post-chain retry applies 2140. Not an order defect against portava-ci: 2140 was committed on 2026-08-23, four days before 2178 existed, and passes there on CI's own CHECK. Not a trip-domain file.

Not an order defect: no position of 2137 replays 2137, 2276-2279 and 2292 all cleanly (measured 2026-10-06, docs/migrations.md § "Apply-order overrides"). Not a trip-domain file.

files.2970_stamp_definitions_evidences_presenc: PRECONDITION FAILED (2970): stamp_definitions is missing slug(s): first_trip_completed, long_haul, weekend_wanderer, international_voyager, solo_traveler, group_tripper, good_host, road_warrior, frequent_flyer, city_explorer, world_citizen, globe_trotter_5, globe_trotter_10, first_trip_created, trip_planner, hidden_gem_explorer, first_postcard, safe_return_ready, safe_return_completed, event_participant, first_event_joined, first_event_hosted, verified_traveler. — A FACT ABOUT THE REPLAY, NOT ABOUT THE FILE, and measured both ways rather than assumed. The slugs are seeded by 0082_stamp_definitions_v2.sql; this harness starts the chain at LOCAL_DB_FROM=2093, so 0082 never runs, and the 2026-08-19 baseline is a STRUCTURE dump — `grep -c "INSERT INTO public.stamp_definitions" baseline/20260819_baseline_structure.sql` returns 0. So the table exists and is EMPTY, and 2970's precondition is doing exactly what it was written for: refusing to record decisions about rows that do not exist. Verified on a local PostgreSQL 16.13: against an empty catalog it raises the error above (exit 3); against a catalog carrying the 23 slugs it APPLIES (exit 0), is idempotent on re-run, and marks 13 of them TRUE — and still emits its own VACUITY WARNING that 23 is short of the 63 this tree seeds. Not a trip-domain file.
